rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline meant to get a finishing run and measurements. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 8 mm apart across the body (x = -0.02 to +0.02 m) at y = 0.05 m ahead of the axle. A 12 mm footprint is narrower than the 25 mm tape, so the tape always covers at least one sensor. Wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.10 x 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg are mid-range values that keep yaw inertia moderate. Controller: sensor weights are proportional to sensor x (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), so a positive signal (line to the left) steers left. kp = 3.0 gives roughly 500 PWM of wheel differential for a 1 cm offset. ki = 0.1 is small to avoid integral windup on curves. kd = 0.3 damps oscillation. base_speed = 1.3 (about 65% of full PWM) is a moderate start, since finishing in 3 s needs about 1.5 m/s average and the first run will show whether this is enough. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot recovers toward the side it was last on. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some weaving on the slalom. Hypotheses to test: (1) the speed is too low to finish in 3 s; (2) kp is too high, causing oscillation (steering_oscillation high); (3) kd is too low for the slalom. Next measurements: completion_time and progress to judge speed, steering_oscillation and max_error to judge gains, line_loss_events to judge sensor coverage.
